headline: Chips Charge Into the Weekend as Software Stumbles; Geopolitical Tension Sets the Table for Monday
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a split note, with 301 names advancing against 241 declining across a universe of 545 securities. Semiconductors led all sectors with a gain of 3.05%, powered by a cluster of standout moves: Sandisk surged 11.9%, Semtech added 9.22%, and both KLA Corp and Marvell Technology rose more than 7%, reflecting broad-based conviction in the chip space rather than any single catalyst.

The enthusiasm stopped firmly at the software aisle. The Software sector shed 1.25%, the worst reading on the board, with Fair Isaac and UiPath each plunging more than 16% — the session's two steepest declines by a wide margin. Autodesk fell 8.26%, PTC dropped 6.04%, and Snowflake slid 5.41%, leaving the group nursing a collective bruise heading into the long weekend. Healthcare also underperformed, off 0.74%, while Energy dipped 0.33% despite OPEC+ electing to hold its October output policy unchanged.

Investors return Monday to a geopolitically charged backdrop: the U.S. military struck three Iranian crude carriers over the weekend, tensions along NATO's eastern perimeter remain elevated following the Leipzig drone incident, and gasoline prices hit a record high over Labor Day. Those crosscurrents — energy supply risk, tightening alliance postures, and a software sector in need of a stabilizing narrative — will define the week's opening tone.

briefs.headline: U.S. Strikes Iranian Crude Carriers, Rattling Energy Markets
briefs.body: American forces hit three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend, according to U.S. Central Command. The action injects fresh uncertainty into crude supply expectations just as OPEC+ confirmed it will leave its October production policy untouched, a combination traders will reprice at Monday's open.

briefs.headline: OPEC+ Holds the Line on October Output
briefs.body: The producer alliance concluded its latest review without adjusting supply targets for next month. The steady-as-she-goes decision had provided modest support to energy equities late in the week, though the sector still closed Friday down 0.33% as demand-growth concerns lingered.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors Sweep the Week's Best Performers
briefs.body: Five of Friday's six top gainers hailed from the semiconductor supply chain, spanning memory, analog, and equipment sub-segments. The breadth of the move — no single name accounting for an outsized share — suggests institutional rotation into the group rather than a stock-specific event.

briefs.headline: Software's Brutal Friday: Two Names Down More Than 16%
briefs.body: Fair Isaac and UiPath each surrendered more than 16% on Friday, the session's sharpest individual declines, dragging the broader Software sector to a 1.25% loss. Autodesk fell an additional 8.26%, leaving the group as the clear laggard and raising questions about near-term earnings visibility across the segment.

briefs.headline: NATO Envoy Warns Against Hybrid Aggression as Leipzig Drone Affair Escalates
briefs.body: A U.S. envoy to NATO stated that the alliance will not accept hybrid attacks on member states, remarks that follow Russia's foreign minister describing Western accusations over the Leipzig drone incident as tantamount to an act of war. The exchange sharpens the geopolitical risk premium for European-linked assets heading into the new week.

briefs.headline: Record Labor Day Pump Prices Add to Consumer Pressure
briefs.body: American motorists faced the highest Labor Day weekend gasoline prices on record, according to reports, piling fresh strain on household budgets. The data point arrives as the Consumer sector posted a modest 0.54% gain on Friday — a resilient number on the surface that may face a sterner test once the fuel-price impact filters through spending data.
